Definition: An open, auditable, code-neutral platform that performs the mechanics and lets the user supply governing code data, material properties, component data, and rule checks.
The computational successor to the classical flexibility-equation approach, modeling the system as connected line elements with six DOF per node.

A user- or organization-supplied data artifact defining the governing code/design basis, required inputs, stress categories, load combinations, formulas, allowable limits, pass/fail criteria, source notes, versioning, checksums, and redistribution status.
Verification requiring code-specific and project-specific information that the responsible engineer or organization must provide.

Synonyms: M. W. Kellogg, Design of Piping Systems (1956); Kellogg tradition
Definition: Classical piping flexibility and stress-analysis treatise (1956) representing the tradition the project is grounded in.
Each node in the global piping model carries six degrees of freedom.
Framing of modern piping stress analysis for the vast majority of piping systems.
User/organization-maintained libraries for valves, flanges, fittings, reducers, expansion joints, supports, and equipment connections; public ones must be lawfully redistributable with provenance.
Per-entry attribution: source, date, contributor, license/permission basis, verification status, and value origin (vendor-specific, measured, calculated, or standard-derived).
Required statement for data and rule contributions that the contributor has the right to submit the material under the project license.
Transparent report sufficient for engineering review and audit, listing versions, model data, results, rule-pack checksum, and signoff.
